handback.t:
W12 (G11) is finished. My verdict is a conditional accept of the additive learned team model only, as an opt-in module. I reject the pairwise term and both gates. Everything is simulation on my own worlds, with no real traces.

**What I built**
- New bin `src/bin/g11_team.rs` plus `src/bin/g11_common/{mod,world,base,learn}.rs`. No `src/*.rs` was touched, no new crates, no commits.
- **Worlds.** They do not share W7's generator: variable requirement-tag sets and noisy graded reward (noise sd 0.2). The primary metric is the noise-free team value `v`.
  - RC: coverage of weighted skill demands, with drift and large variants.
  - ROLE: 3 of 5 roles needed, plus a duplicate-role penalty.
  - THR: capability thresholds, near-additive.
  - LAT: additive plus pairwise by construction, so not independent evidence.
  - Two separable controls, C-SEP and C-SEPT; C-SEPT has a trap keyword map.
  - Set 1 (the eight worlds above) was frozen before any policy ran.
  - Set 2 is keyword-degraded copies of those worlds. I added it after the first dev run showed a perfect keyword table is close to the oracle in RC and ROLE.
  - Set 3 is COMP and COMP-X (hidden complementary pairs), added later.
- **Arms.** L-add (additive), L-pair (additive plus pairwise), L-gate (pair model used only when a prequential test favours it), and L-full (L-gate plus a causal controller gate between the learner and `seq:guarded-safe`).
- **Baselines.** Sequential routers with team credit, tuned per world on seeds 1-8, plus `NeuralMesh` with `team_size=K`. The best fair baseline is picked on the evaluation seeds, which is conservative.
- **Protocol.** Tuning on seeds 1-8 only, held 31-60, fresh confirm 61-90, and `--tune perworld` as the generous check. Paired 95% t-CI, Holm applied separately within each world set. Controls get TOST ±0.01 plus a one-sided non-inferiority test, and there is a reward-noise sensitivity run (`--noise 0.1` and `0.4`).

**Results for L-add** (difference in `v` vs the best fair baseline; held and confirm agree)

- **Set 2 (keyword table half wrong):** Holm wins in every world, and the sign is the same across held, confirm and per-world tuning.

  | World | Diff vs best fair |
  |---|---|
  | RC-K | about +0.065 |
  | RC-L-K | +0.08 |
  | ROLE-K | about +0.11 |
  | THR-K | +0.09 to +0.14 |

- **Set 1:**
  - THR +0.14 to +0.16, a win, but it is a near-additive world.
  - RC-drift +0.015 to +0.021, a win.
  - It loses to a perfect keyword table: RC −0.014, RC-L −0.007, ROLE −0.009 to −0.011. The per-world-tuned runs shrink these to −0.004 to −0.011, or n.s. for ROLE.
  - Against the repo default `seq:guarded-safe` the same worlds are RC −0.011, RC-L −0.002, ROLE +0.113.
- **Set 3:** COMP +0.09 to +0.10 and COMP-X +0.076, both wins. COMP-X was built to defeat a global pairwise term and did not hurt the additive model.
- **Generators with a Holm win:** set 1 gets RC (drift only) and THR; set 2 gets RC, ROLE and THR; set 3 gets COMP and COMP-X. Excluding the near-additive THR and the pairwise-by-construction LAT, that is RC-drift only in set 1 and RC and ROLE in set 2.
- **vs `mesh(guarded-safe)`:** +0.05 to +0.33 in every world, all Holm wins.

**Pairwise term and gates**
- **L-pair vs L-add:** worse in the RC family (−0.007 to −0.016) and in ROLE on held. It is better only in pairwise-by-construction worlds, and not robustly: LAT is better only on confirm, and COMP and COMP-X are n.s. after Holm.
- **L-gate:** inert, within 0.0012 of L-add everywhere.
- **L-full (controller gate):** costs 1 to 4 points where the learner helps, for example THR −0.041 and ROLE-K −0.026. With q=0.2 and T=2500 there are about 250 randomized decisions per arm and reward sd about 0.23, so the standard error of the arm difference is about 0.021. By arithmetic, the gate cannot resolve the 0.01 to 0.02 gaps at stake.

**Separable controls and harmlessness**
- The W7 control regression is fixed at noise 0.2, but by a count-based step boost I found on dev seeds, not by gating. C-SEP is +0.045 to +0.053. C-SEPT is +0.005 and n.s., and non-inferior (Holm 0.004 to 0.010).
- TOST ±0.01 is not shown in any of the 8 control cells. For C-SEP the learner is better than the margin; for C-SEPT the paired seed sd makes the CI wider than the margin.
- Harmlessness is not noise-robust. C-SEPT becomes a Holm loss at noise 0.4 (−0.033) and at 0.1 (−0.017). At noise 0.4 the set-1 losses to the perfect keyword table also grow (RC −0.031, RC-L −0.024, ROLE −0.038).

**Cost** (single thread, policy only)

| Policy | ns/decision | Heap bytes |
|---|---|---|
| L-add | 0.4 to 1.2 µs | 5.7 to 15.8 KB |
| `mesh(guarded-safe)` | 2.9 to 8.1 µs | 11 to 24 KB |
| `seq:guarded-safe` | 5.7 to 27.7 µs | 9.6 to 16.9 KB |
| L-full | 3 to 22 µs | 21 to 55 KB |

**Caveats**
- The set-2 and set-3 evidence was added after I had seen set-1 dev results.
- The sequential baselines credit every member with the whole team reward, and a difference-reward baseline was not tried.
- I looked at the held/confirm numbers of the 14-world version once before adding COMP, COMP-X, the non-inferiority test, the ablation and `--noise`. The learner and worlds 1-14 were unchanged afterwards, and the pooled tuning picked the same configs. All reported numbers come from the final binary.
- `results/g11_team_dev.*` is from a mid-development binary; do not cite it.
